agree.reason: Opening on traffic, conceding the C-to-D drop and adding that the speaker will pay that cost too, makes the speech credible to the two traffic-focused commissioners, but it offers nothing that reduces the traffic, so opposing neighbours and those commissioners get a trade-off to accept rather than a reason to stop worrying.

honest.reason: Every number matches the brief, but 'the people who live there will park on that lot, not on our street' claims more than 72 spaces can guarantee, and '64 families who stop waiting' assumes the tenants all come from the waiting list.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out that 64 homes is about one for every six households on the 412-household list and that 72 spaces is more than one per home, but it leaves the 310 trips as a raw daily total instead of breaking them down per hour or per rush-hour period, which would have been their most favourable true form.

right_comparison.reason: It states the alternative plainly, as the facts show it: the lot stays empty six days a week and the three-year wait stays where it is, and it sets that against the rush-hour D.

qualification.reason: The speech makes no claim that depends on an uncertain future result, and its one concession, that 64 homes doesn't close a gap of 2,100, needs no checkable condition.

objections.reason: It meets the traffic objection head-on and answers parking, which neighbours are likely to raise, but its answer to traffic is to say the cost is worth it, with no attempt to show the 310 trips are smaller than they sound.

fit.reason: At roughly 400 words in short spoken sentences, with the speaker's stake disclosed and a clear ask, it fits the three-minute public-comment format well.
